query: Longer Each Night Lyra wants you in the duel hall after hours. "You let it go too early," she says, and lights her own. "Hold it. Longer each night. It will bite you; let it." Hold it until it bites You hold it until the heat is in your teeth and then a breath longer. When you let it go it runs to the rafters. Lyra looks at your blistered palm and says nothing, which is approval. Ask her how she stands it She doesn't answer at first. Then she shows you her palms, scarred and old, and tells you about the first time, and her mother. You don't practise much. It's still the right night.

Let It Run
Lyra lets you into the duel hall after it has closed. She cups her hands and the fire in them grows, and grows, until it lights the rafters. "They taught me to keep it small," she says. "This is what it does when I stop. I've never shown anyone."

One Last Duel
Dawn, the empty dueling ring, no crowd. Lyra is waiting. "No referee," she says. "No points. Just one last duel, for us. So we know."
